newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH HARVEST FLOOD DAMAGE AT LEAST CZK 1.5BLN.
newsitem.headline: CZECH HARVEST FLOOD DAMAGE AT LEAST CZK 1.5BLN.

text.p: The Czech Agriculture Ministry on Friday said preliminary estimates on harvest damage from massive flooding in the eastern part of the country was about 1.5 billion crowns.
"So far the figure is 1.5 billion crowns in damages to the harvest," ministry official Marcela Dvorakova told Reuters, adding that more information would be collected and released on Tuesday.

Milos Kordac, assistent to the president of the Czech Agrarian Chamber said data collected from most of the affected districts so far put damage to harvests at least at 1.4 billion crowns, with about 130,000 hectares of agricultural land affected.
"Damages on agricultures so far is some 1.4 billion crowns, and 600 million on property," he told Reuters.
When asked whether the situation would lead to a significant increase in imports, Kordac said: "We think not. The damage is not so large as to deteriorate the balance of the market."
However, he added that reports have not yet been delivered from some hard-hit areas where phones don't work or farmers have not yet had chance to inspect their land.
Both said the figure excluded damage to fields due to mud, erosion and other factors.
The flooding, which is reported to have claimed at least 32 lives, was moving further south on Friday while water levels were coming down on upper streams of the affected rivers.
Poland, Slovakia amd Austria have also been hit by the rain-induced flooding.

Some of the thousands of evacuated have started returning home in the north-eastern city of Ostrava and others, the local news agency CTK reported, while emergency operations continued in the south-east.
